- Requirement: The PR's stated intent (last-commit summary and changelog fragment) is "fully qualify the changelog push and fetch refspecs so stable releases stop dropping the changelog" — i.e. ship the fix and prevent its regression. The contract assertions added to tests/test_changelog_fragment_contract.py::test_release_assembly_fails_open are the regression guard.
  Expected change site: Either (a) a step in .github/workflows/ci.yml that runs tests/test_changelog_fragment_contract.py, alongside the existing "Mark-stable release-tag refspec contract test" step at ci.yml:832-835 that runs tests/test_mark_stable_release_tag_refspec_contract.py; or (b) the new refspec assertions should live in tests/test_mark_stable_release_tag_refspec_contract.py (which IS in CI) instead of tests/test_changelog_fragment_contract.py (which is not).
  Evidence of absence: I searched every CI workflow for `tests/test_changelog_fragment_contract.py` (ci.yml, mark-stable.yml, test-and-mark-stable.yml) — there are zero invocations. The test file is also not in any `pytest tests/...` discovery invocation; CI uses targeted `python3 tests/<name>.py` and `python3 -m pytest -q tests/<name>.py` calls, all of which name specific files. The new refspec assertions therefore never execute in CI; a future edit that reverts the qualified forms back to bare `HEAD:${SOURCE_BRANCH}` / `git fetch origin ${SOURCE_BRANCH}` would not be caught by the contract test because the contract test does not run. This is also a real regression risk because the only other mechanism that would catch the bug is the live release-gate run itself, which only happens during an actual stable release (run 35570966035 last caught it after 113 fragments went unfolded). PR #4210's analogous test on main likely faces the same gap, but this PR is duplicating that gap on the stable branch instead of fixing it.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- Requirement: The PR's stated intent is "fully qualify the changelog push and fetch refspecs so stable releases stop dropping the changelog" — fix the bug AND lock it in against regression. The new assertions added to tests/test_changelog_fragment_contract.py::test_release_assembly_fails_open at tests/test_changelog_fragment_contract.py:210-219 are the regression guard.
  Expected change site: Either (a) a step in .github/workflows/ci.yml alongside the existing "Mark-stable release-tag refspec contract test" step at ci.yml:832-835 that runs PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 python3 tests/test_changelog_fragment_contract.py; or (b) move the four new refspec assertions into tests/test_mark_stable_release_tag_refspec_contract.py (which IS in CI) so they execute on every PR / push.
  Evidence of absence: I searched every CI workflow (ci.yml, mark-stable.yml, test-and-mark-stable.yml) and every shell script and Python file for "test_changelog_fragment_contract" — there are zero invocations. CI uses targeted `python3 tests/<name>.py` calls (each test file is named explicitly) and there is no `pytest tests/` discovery invocation; the test file is therefore unreachable from CI. Concretely, a future edit that reverts mark-stable.yml:607 / test-and-mark-stable.yml:5086 back to `git push origin "HEAD:${SOURCE_BRANCH}"` or that reverts the two `git fetch origin "+refs/heads/${SOURCE_BRANCH}:refs/remotes/origin/${SOURCE_BRANCH}"` calls back to bare `git fetch origin "${SOURCE_BRANCH}"` would not be caught by the contract test because the contract test never runs. The bug was previously caught only when the actual release-gate run fired (run 35570966035, which left 113 fragments unfolded); without the test running in CI, the same regression would only be caught at the next release rather than at PR-review time. PR #4210's analogous test on main may face the same gap, but this PR is propagating that gap onto the stable branch instead of closing it.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
